_comment: Every fabric command a session is told to run, by the name it runs under. bootstrap.sh links each into ~/.local/bin (on every account's PATH) and user-settings.py allows each by a narrow `Bash(<name> *)` rule in the account's user settings, so neither the path nor the approval depends on where a session starts. A skill, a hook message or a project snippet names these, never `$AGENT_FABRIC_ROOT/...`: the harness asks before any command that carries a shell expansion, whatever the mode or the rules, and a Monitor re-armed every thirty minutes asked every time (the owner, 2026-09-26: no approval for any fabric script or executable). A new session-facing command is added here, in the same change that tells a session to run it. A command in `not_allowed` is linked like the others but gets no allow rule, with the reason beside it: a wrapper that runs another command would carry an approval for every command it can run.

replaces._comment: A command's earlier target, which bootstrap recognises as a link it made and moves to the current one; without it an account keeps the old link, the allow rule is withheld (user-settings.py) and every use asks. The GZCoord commands were Node shims until their Python entry points.

not_allowed.fabric-genimage: every run spends on the OpenAI account (the owner, 2026-10-07): a person approves each one, so no session spends unattended
not_allowed.fabric-lease: runs whatever command follows `--`: an allow rule for it would allow every command, so it asks as any command does
not_allowed.fabric-resume: starts a session: it is run in an account's shell by a person or by moveto --resume, never by a session, so no allow rule
not_allowed.fabric-watch: a status pane's loop until q, started by moveto --watch in an account's pane, never by a session: an allow rule would let a session hang on it
not_allowed.fabric-secret-run: runs whatever command follows `--`, with the agent's own secrets in its environment: an allow rule would allow every command, so it asks as any command does
not_allowed.fabric-host: `run` executes any command on a host as any account (the operator's instrument): allowing it would allow everything
